record.context_brief: Graph energy lower bound via independence number
record.original_question: If G is a graph on n vertices with independence number alpha, must the sum of the positive adjacency eigenvalues satisfy sum_{lambda_i(G) > 0} lambda_i(G) >= n - alpha?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 20 ([11]). Let G be a graph on n vertices with independence number α. Then sum_{λ_i(G)>0} λ_i(G) ≥ n − α.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\lambda_1(G) \ge \lambda_2(G) \ge \cdots \ge \lambda_n(G)$ denote the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. Let $\alpha(G)$ denote the independence number of $G$, i.e., the maximum size of a set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices. Prove or disprove that
$$\sum_{\lambda_i(G) > 0} \lambda_i(G) \;\ge\; n - \alpha(G).$$
(Equivalently, since the sum of all eigenvalues is zero, this asserts that the graph energy $E(G) = \sum_i |\lambda_i(G)|$ satisfies $E(G) \ge 2(n-\alpha(G))$.)
artifact.status_search_result: This is a long-standing conjecture of Fajtlowicz (Graffiti, 1980s), equivalent to E(G) ≥ 2(n - α(G)). It has been verified computationally for all graphs on up to 10 vertices and holds for almost all graphs, as well as for several special classes (graphs meeting Hoffman's ratio bound, graphs with α(G) = χ_f(complement), etc.), but the general conjecture remains open as of recent literature (2024–2025).

status_evidence.title: A graph energy conjecture through the lenses of semidefinite programming
status_evidence.snippet: Fajtlowicz conjectured in the 1980s that 1/2·E(G) ≥ n − α(G); verified for graphs up to 10 vertices and for several classes.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture is open in general but proven for several classes.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved Problems in Spectral Graph Theory
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open conjecture in a survey of unsolved spectral graph problems.
